correctness.rationale: For every real SPD 2x2 input, the Gaussian angle reduction, determinant lemma and rank-one log-M spectrum give E(error²)=2E(Z²). A uniform Fourier expansion and Parseval give the exact dilogarithm identity. The strict baseline comparison follows from the top eigenvalue bound on trace(Ahat) with equality characterized. The scaled Cauchy representation and an explicitly integrable majorant justify dominated convergence and the exact coefficient 8[log(1+b)+2log2] for each fixed b>0. Independently executed verification confirms 100 integral values, 480 matrix-and-Lanczos reconstructions and four asymptotic scales; it is corroboration rather than proof.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant 2026 preconditioned one-probe method and conditional trace-variance identity are acknowledged. The inspected source supplies general Nyström bounds for larger oversampled ranks, not the exact unconditional two-eigenvalue risk and its sharp inverse-square-root high-contrast coefficient. The distinct 2017 subspace-iteration log-determinant estimator and 2023 randomized matrix-function approximation do not imply this complete result without new distributional analysis. Targeted literature and mathematical-finding searches returned no statement-equivalent result; remaining unindexed-equivalence risk is named.

value.rationale: The exact unconditional risk for the recently proposed Gaussian Nyström one-probe log-determinant estimator is a natural, previously unquantified benchmark. It resolves the complete two-eigenvalue case, including a strict loss relative to ideal spectral rank-one preconditioning, and a sharp inverse-square-root spectral-gap penalty caused by rare Gaussian sketch directions. This precise cutoff informs how quickly preconditioning randomness vanishes with spectral separation, without claiming broader dimensional performance.
